candidate.blueprint_locator: Basic Care and Comfort — mobility, positioning, transfer, and assistive-device use
candidate.blueprint_topic: Basic Care and Comfort — safe patient handling
candidate.educational_objective: Use patient-specific mobility assessment to select safe handling equipment and techniques.

options.A: To prescribe one handling method for every client without reassessment.
options.B: To document staff injury only after a transfer has already occurred.
options.C: To assess the client's mobility and handling needs and select appropriate equipment and techniques.
options.D: To determine handling methods only for clients with bariatric body size.

candidate.rationale: OSHA states that each patient has unique abilities that should be systematically assessed, with emphasis on mobility, so caregivers can determine the safest equipment and techniques for handling and movement. Safe patient handling applies across patient populations, not only to bariatric clients. C is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Each patient's mobility and abilities should be assessed to determine the safest equipment and techniques for handling and movement; safe patient handling programs apply broadly in healthcare.
candidate.source_document_title: Worker Safety in Hospitals — Facility and Patient Needs Assessment; Safe Patient Handling
candidate.source_locator: Patient Needs Assessments and Algorithms; Safe Patient Handling program elements
candidate.stem: What is the purpose of a safe patient-handling assessment or algorithm before transferring or repositioning a client?
